newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc dives from seven-year highs.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc dives from seven-year highs.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three month zinc dived on Tuesday morning on fund selling and general liquidation, losing $170 a tonne in the space of about 30 minutes, traders said.
"Inventors started panicking this morning. They were getting scared when the price was getting too far ahead of the fundamentals," an analyst said.

The three month price was indicated much of the morning around $1,660, just below a seven-year high of $1,674 hit on Monday and a touch off Monday's kerb close of $1,671. But at around 0900 GMT it crumbled, sliding to $1,480/$1,500.

Waves of speculative buying had sent the market sky-rocketing in recent days on the back of news that Chinese smelters had sold forward about 250,000 tonnes at low prices last year and needed to cover by September.
Prices had gained $125, or eight percent, in the last three days alone.
Many traders and analysts had been warning the three months market was overheated and needed a correction, but the speed of the decline caught the market by surprise.
"It was massively over-extended...once it started there were no buyers at all, just sellers," one trader said.

One analyst said prices could easily fall to $1,400 now that speculative steam was leaving the market and LME stocks were not at critical levels. The future price outlook hinged in large part on how much the Chinese short position had already been covered, analysts said.
On Monday, a senior Chinese industry source said between a half and two-thirds of the Zhuzhou smelter's estimated 90,000 tonnes of short positions had already been covered.
A main focus in later LME ring trading would be the spreads. The premium of cash over three months was indicated at $90/$100, unchanged from Monday evening levels.
Other markets were only slightly affected by zinc's move.
Aluminium was marginally weaker at $1,674, down $16 from Monday.
Analysts said prices might consolidate under $1,700 after hitting a year's high of $1,711 on Monday.
Copper had already eased early on Tuesday, and as zinc slid it eased to a low of $2,312, compared to Monday's close of $2,353. But it rebounded to be last indicated at $2,338/43.
A stocks rise of 6,475 tonnes brings the July increase to 95,450 tonnes and offers the prospect of seeing July hit 100,000 tonnes, analyst Nick Moore of Flemings Global Mining Group said.
"This would be the biggest monthly rise since at least 1975," he said.
Comex stocks rose by 3,316 short tons on Monday, ending a series of falls.
Nickel declined to $7,290, a support level and down $105 from Monday.
Next support was pegged at $7,220.
Lead was little changed at $640, up $3, and tin was $10 softer at $5,390.
Alloy was at $1,510 versus $1,510/20.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
